content.comment_body: Hello, I'm facing trouble programming the [product_name] controller to read accurate temperature and humidity values from a 4-20mA sensor. I've reviewed forum discussions on analog scaling but still need help. My setup: - [product_name] controller, model [article_no] 12/24RCE - STEGO sensor CSS 014, model no. 01420.2-00 (4-20mA TEMP -40°C to +60°C / 0 to 100% RH) Both analog inputs are wired to terminals 7 for temperature (AI1) and 8 for humidity (AI2), each with a 220 Ohm resistor between input and power supply negative. Currently, the display shows AI1 as 317 and AI2 as 177. I'm unable to get practical values like 20°C or 20% humidity. I suspect an analog amplifier is needed, but I may not be setting the block correctly. Any advice is appreciated.
Regarding the 220 Ohm resistor setup: Could you share a [url] to the manual, especially referencing any pages that explain this specific resistor configuration?

You should observe something on your [product_name] controller's display. Please upload your program for review. Is your sensor definitely a 4-20mA type? In that case, a 500 Ohm resistor parallel to the analog input and ground (M) is needed. For scaling in [product_name] software: set up an analog amplifier block with 4-20 mA sensor, for temperature (min -40, max +60) and humidity (min 0, max 100). Using a 220 Ohm resistor results in a sensor span that is approximately 2.7 times higher than with 500 Ohm. With 220 Ohms, scale temp: min -40, max +233; for humidity: min 0, max 270 in [product_name] software.
The use of 200 Ohm resistors is incorrect; you should use 500 Ohm instead. For proper scaling instructions, see attached [document].

[user_name]: Thanks for your reply. Here's the data sheet for my sensor—not the I/O link type shown in the second image: [url]. Technical support sent a picture for connection assistance, and I'll attach it here. Although it's not high-quality, you can see the wiring if enlarged.
[user_name], thanks for sharing your program—I’ll test it as soon as I receive my 500 Ohm resistors. I appreciate you taking time to respond and will follow up with feedback soon.
